blocks.prompt: 13. The motion of a robotic arm moving along a straight track is described by the velocity function \(v(t) = 6 + t - t^2\) where \(v(t)\) is in meters per second and \(t\) is the time in seconds, valid for \(0 \le t \le 5\). Find the distance travelled by the arm.
blocks.explanation:
Distance (not displacement) from a velocity function: it is the total area between the v-t graph and the t-axis.
Given: \(v(t)\) on \(0 \le t \le 5\). Find: the total distance.
Plan: find where \(v = 0\), integrate \(v\) on each piece, and add the areas as positive amounts (the book's Note: distance \(= A_1 + A_2\)).
steps:
Given: \(v(t) = 6 + t - t^2\) m/s for \(0 \le t \le 5\).
To find: the distance travelled by the arm.
Method: The area under the v-t graph is the displacement; when the graph goes below the t-axis, the book's Note says displacement \(= A_1 - A_2\) but distance \(= A_1 + A_2\). So we find where the velocity changes sign and integrate on each interval.

Where is v = 0?
\[6 + t - t^2 = 0\]
\[t^2 - t - 6 = 0\]
\[(t - 3)(t + 2) = 0\]
\[t = 3\quad (t = -2\ \text{rejected})\]
Why: The arm can change direction only where \(v = 0\); \(t = -2\) is outside \(0 \le t \le 5\).

Sign of v on each interval
\[v(0) = 6 > 0,\quad v(4) = -6 < 0\]
Why: \(v = -(t - 3)(t + 2)\) is positive for \(0 \le t < 3\) (moving forward) and negative for \(3 < t \le 5\) (moving back).

Integral on each interval
\[\int_0^3 v\,dt = \dfrac{27}{2} - 0 = \dfrac{27}{2}\]
\[\int_3^5 v\,dt = \dfrac{5}{6} - \dfrac{27}{2} = -\dfrac{38}{3}\]
\[A_1 = \dfrac{27}{2},\quad A_2 = \dfrac{38}{3}\]
Why: \(\frac{5}{6} - \frac{81}{6} = -\frac{76}{6}\). The second integral is negative because the graph is below the t-axis there; the area is its size.

Total distance
\[\text{Distance} = \dfrac{27}{2} + \dfrac{38}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{81 + 76}{6} = \dfrac{157}{6}\]
\[\approx 26.17\ \text{m}\]
Why: Distance \(= A_1 + A_2\), both counted as positive.

Check
\[A_1 - A_2 = \dfrac{81 - 76}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}\]
\[F(5) - F(0) = \dfrac{5}{6}\ \checkmark\]
Why: \(A_1 - A_2\) is the displacement, and it matches \(\int_0^5 v\,dt\). The arm went 13.5 m forward and about 12.67 m back, ending only 5/6 m from the start.
blocks.final_answer: Distance travelled \(= \frac{157}{6} \approx 26.17\) m (the displacement is only \(\frac{5}{6}\) m).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The book prints no answer for Exercise 7.1, so this answer is ours. It was checked independently with a computer algebra system and against an independent worked solution. Common mistake: \(\int_0^5 v\,dt = \frac{5}{6}\) m is the displacement, not the distance; split the integral at every point where \(v = 0\).
